docs.title: Class: Event
docs.text:
This class comprises distinct, delimited and coherent processes and

interactions of a material nature, in cultural, social or physical

systems, involving and affecting instances of E77 Persistent Item in a

way characteristic of the kind of process. Typical examples are meetings,

births, deaths, actions of decision taking, making or inventing things,

but also more complex and extended ones such as conferences, elections,

building of a castle, or battles.

__

While the continuous growth of a tree lacks the limits characteristic of

an event, its germination from a seed does qualify as an event.

Similarly, the blowing of the wind lacks the distinctness and limits of

an event, but a hurricane, flood or earthquake would qualify as an event.

Mental processes are considered as events, in cases where they are

connected with the material externalization of their results; for

example, the creation of a poem, a performance or a change of intention

that becomes obvious from subsequent actions or declarations.

__

The effects of an instance of E5 Event may not lead to relevant permanent

changes of properties or relations of the items involved in it, for

example an unrecorded performance. Of course, in order to be documented,

some kind of evidence for an event must exist, be it witnesses, traces or

products of the event.

__

While instances of E4 Period always require some form of coherence

between its constituent phenomena, in addition, the essential

constituents of instances of E5 Event should contribute to an overall

effect; for example, the statements made during a meeting and the

listening of the audience.

__

Viewed at a coarse level of detail, an instance of E5 Event may appear as

if it had an ‘instantaneous’ overall effect, but any process or

interaction of material nature in reality have an extent in time and

space. At a fine level, instances of E5 Event may be analysed into

component phenomena and phases within a space and timeframe, and as such

can be seen as a period, regardless of the size of the phenomena. The

reverse is not necessarily the case: not all instances of E4 Period give

rise to a noteworthy overall effect and are thus not instances of E5

Event.

__

docs.title: Enum: MaterialTechType
docs.text:
The physical matter or substance from which an object is made, including

any tangible substances, either naturally or synthetically derived,

ranging from specific materials to types of material designated by their

function. The term comprises both the media that are incorporated in an

object and any support to which the media are applied.

__

Based on AAT "materials (matter)";

CDWA "Materials/Techniques"

__

Use the most specific term for the material that is appropriate. It is

strongly recommended to take the indexing term from a published

controlled vocabulary, preferably a Linked Open Vocabulary, for example

the Art & Architecture Thesaurus, specifically its

Materials hierarchy.

__

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

__

Medium, as a value for the type attribute of the LIDO Term

Materials/Techniques element, designates the material that is applied to

a support in the making of an object or a work of art, such as ink on

paper or oil paint on canvas; often a particular technique or techniques

are closely associated with the media.

Based on AAT "media (artists' materials)";

CDWA Materials/Techniques.

__

In many forms of art, a distinction is made between materials used as the

media, and materials used as the support. Medium is the material applied

to the support. For example, for a drawing described as pen and brown ink

and black chalk on paper, pen is the instrument, ink and black chalk are

the media, and paper is the support. [Cited from Categories for the

Description of Works of Art (CDWA) "Materials/Techniques"]

__

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

__

Support, as a value for the type attribute of the LIDO Term

Materials/Techniques element, designates the surface material to which

media are applied or a work is mounted, for example canvas, oak panel,

laid paper, wood, copper, glass, or marble. For example, with paintings,

drawings, prints, or photographs, the media would be applied to the

surface of a support such as paper, wood panel, canvas, or glass in order

to create the image. Used typically for two-dimensional works, although

the concept may apply to any work.

__

Based on AAT "supports";

CDWA "Materials/Techniques"

__

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

__

Record a term specifying the color, tint, or hue of the material,

particularly if color is an unusual or important characteristic of the

object. [All colored impressions of materials of an object are meant, not

just parts treated with dyestuff. The information refers to the overall

effect of color, not only as cause of, e.g., dyeing or painting.]

__

It is recommended to use internationally approved standard color charts,

codes and terminology such as the Universal Color Language (UCL). Use

preferably color names as specified by the Art & Architecture Thesaurus

(AAT). Centroid color numbers, which refer to the appropriate

color-blocks on the

Inter-Society Color Council and National Bureau of Standards (ISCC-NBS) color name charts,

are also provided by the AAT.

__

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

__

Implement, as a value for the type attribute of the LIDO Term

Materials/Techniques element, designates any object used to carry out the

technique in order to create or modify an object, including equipment,

tools, apparatus, utensils, instruments, and other things employed in any

trade or used in executing a task or work.

__

Based on

CDWA "Materials/Techniques";

AAT "implements"

__

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

__

Technique, as a value for the type attribute of the LIDO Term

Materials/Techniques element, designates the manner, method, or process

applied in the creation, design, or modification of an object.

__

Based on CDWA "Materials/Techniques".

__

Use the most specific term for indexing that is appropriate. It is

strongly recommended to take the indexing term from a published

controlled vocabulary, preferably a

Linked Open Vocabulary, for example

the Art & Architecture Thesaurus, specifically its

Processes and Techniques hierarchy.

__

For information about scientific methods by which an object was found or

collected, such as field collection methods in archaeology, use the LIDO

Event Method element.

__

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

__

Watermark, as a value for the type attribute of the LIDO Term

Materials/Techniques element, designates an identification of the

watermark type or name. A watermark is a design incorporated into paper

as it is made, typically a sign of the manufacturer, or a proof of

authenticity for documents and banknotes. The mark is visible through

transmitted light, appearing as translucent or shaded area.

__

Based on CDWA "Materials/Techniques";

AAT "watermarks"

__

It is recommended to use as indexing terms descriptors of internationally

or nationally approved classifications, such as the

Watermark Information System,

the Index of watermark classes and subclasses,

provided as a

Registration Standard of the

International Association of Paper Historians (IPH),

or the Watermark Descriptor Tables,

provided by the

Thomas L. Gravell Watermark Archive.

__

docs.title: Class: Measurements
docs.text:
O campo description permite uma representação textual das medidas da

edificação, caso não seja possível cadastrar medidas individuais com

precisão, ou seja preciso maior flexibilidade para explicar as dimensões.

__

O campo measurements admite uma lista de medidas com os campos :

__

* type (obrigatório) designa a natureza da medida : largura, altura,

_ área, etc. — usar um dos tipos de dimensões_

_ do Art and Architecture Thesaurus do Instituto Getty (AAT) ;_

* value (obrigatório) valor numérico, usar ponto como separador decimal ;

* unit (obrigatório) uma uri remetendo a uma unidade na

_ hierarquia de unidades de medida_

_ do AAT, ou do nosso próprio [vocabulário controlado] ;_

* extent (opcional) indica a parte do objeto que está sendo medida — por

_ exemplo, se a altura é até a linha de coroamento ou até a cumeeira, etc. —_

_ usar a uri de um vocabulário controlado ;_

* qualifier (opcional) indica que as medidas são aproximadas : usar um

_ qualificador do AAT ;_

* shape (opcional) caso relevante, indicar a forma do elemento medido

_ usando a lista de formas do AAT ;_

__

docs.title: Class: Thing
docs.text:
This class comprises all things in the universe of discourse of the CIDOC

Conceptual Reference Model.

__

It is an abstract concept providing for three general properties:

__

- Identification by name or appellation, and in particular by a preferred

identifier

__

- Classification by type, allowing further refinement of the specific

subclass to which an instance belongs

__

- Attachment of free text and other unstructured data for the expression

of anything not captured by formal properties

__

All other classes within the CIDOC CRM are directly or indirectly

specialisations of E1 CRM Entity.

__

CIDOC–CRM E22 HUMAN-MADE OBJECT

__

This class comprises all persistent physical objects of any size that are

purposely created by human activity and have physical boundaries that

separate them completely in an objective way from other objects.

__

The class also includes all aggregates of objects made for functional

purposes of whatever kind, independent of physical coherence, such as a

set of chessmen.

__

Nos Documentários da Arquitetura Tradicional, esta ficha pode ser usada

para cadastrar uma edificação, um conjunto arquitetônico, ou ainda

uma parte significativa de uma edificação.

__

docs.text: Narrative body content. In the Markdown adapter this corresponds to the document body after YAML frontmatter.

docs.title: Slot: credit
docs.text: Informação sobre autoria ou responsabilidade.

docs.title: Slot: culture
docs.text: An index element for the cultural context from which the object/work in focus originated. Used if the creator or producer is unknown, or if the cultural context is of particular interest. Examples may include the name of a culture, a nation, or an ethnic group.

docs.title: Slot: description
docs.text: A human-readable description for a thing

docs.title: Slot: extent
docs.text: Polygonal, multipolygonal, or linear geographic extent associated with the place.

docs.title: Slot: href
docs.text: Um hyperlink simples.

docs.title: Slot: id
docs.text: Unique identifier for this object.

docs.title: Slot: identifiers
docs.text: Published or external identifiers for the object.

docs.title: Slot: inscriptions
docs.text: Marcas, símbolos ou textos gravados na edificação, especialmente aqueles referentes à estrutura como um todo e não específicos a alguma de suas partes. Não usar para iconografia.

docs.title: Slot: location
docs.text: Representative point location for the place, normally in EPSG:4326 (WGS 84).

docs.title: Slot: location_historic
docs.text: Antigas jurisdições ou designações para o lugar onde o objeto se encontra. Para um sítio de onde o objeto foi fisicamente removido, usar spatial: former_site:.

docs.title: Slot: media_alt
docs.text: Texto alternativo para leitores de tela ou outras formas de acessibilidade. Apenas texto sem formatação.

docs.title: Slot: method
docs.text: An index element for the method by which the event is or was carried out. Examples may include an acquisition method or a field collection method.

docs.title: Slot: object_type
docs.text: An index element for the particular kind of object or work in focus.

docs.title: Slot: part_of
docs.text: Parent place in an administrative, geographic, or historical hierarchy.

docs.title: Slot: place
docs.text: A set of structured information indicating the place or location where an object/work was associated with a particular event.

docs.title: Slot: place_function
docs.text: Function or administrative role of the place, such as municipality seat, state capital, or federal capital.

docs.title: Slot: place_type
docs.text: Classification of the kind of place, such as inhabited place, rural agglomeration, town, city, or municipality.

docs.title: Slot: record_date
docs.text: Date the record was created or last substantively revised.

docs.title: Slot: refid
docs.text: Local or external identifier.

docs.title: Slot: related_events
docs.text: A set of structured information about an event related to the event in focus, indicating the type of relationship where applicable.

docs.title: Slot: style_period
docs.text:
An index element for the period in which the event happened,

comprising information about geologic time scale, archaelogical,

historical, or artistic period, style, or art movement, whose

characteristics are represented by the object or work.

__

Note that "Period/Style" corresponds to "Style" in CDWA as shorthand

for Style/Period/Group/Movement/Dynasty.

__

Examples may be Neolithic for a period, Impressionist for a style, or

Cubism for a movement.

__

docs.title: Slot: subject
docs.text:
Recomenda-se articular o tema em três níveis : descrição, identificação e

interpretação.

__

DESCRIÇÃO se refere a elementos imediatamente reconhecíveis sem

necessidade de conhecimento especializado : coluna(ta)s, arcadas,

brasões, cunhais, ornamentos em geral.

__

IDENTIFICAÇÃO se refere ao reconhecimento das particularidades

arquitetônicas ou iconográficas dos elementos : p. ex. as colunas são da

ordem toscana, a abóbada é de aresta, o brasão pertence a tal família...

__

INTERPRETAÇÃO diz respeito ao significado iconológico, alegórico ou

político dos elementos, incluindo questões de status e estilo.

__

docs.title: Slot: tags
docs.text: Provisional uncontrolled keywords. Prefer classifications or subject for curated vocabulary terms.

docs.title: Slot: temporal
docs.text: Temporalidade do objeto.

docs.title: Slot: term
docs.text: LIDO terminology term.

docs.title: Slot: things_present
docs.text: A set of structured information for a related object or work that is or was present at the event in focus. Repeated if there are multiple related objects or works.

docs.title: Slot: title
docs.text: The preferred human-readable label for a Thing.

docs.title: Slot: title_preference
docs.text: Indica se o nome em questão deve ser oculto ou não, se é uma versão alternativa ou uma variante de grafia, etc.

docs.title: Slot: title_source
docs.text:
📚 A fonte do título title_source é opcional ; um título pode ser atestado em mais de uma fonte, por isso este campo é uma lista de itens (cada item começa com um hífen).

Se a fonte for cadastrada, o campo refid deve conter a chave de citação (citation key) que consta do registro bibliográfico na biblioteca do nosso projeto de pesquisa no Zotero. Em geral, a chave de citação é o DOI ou ISBN da publicação, mas pode ser diferente.

Se necessário, incluir no campo note uma especificação adicional, como o número da página da referência bibliográfica de onde a informação foi extraída.

Todos os campos source no restante da ficha devem ser preenchidos do mesmo modo. (Equivalente DublinCore: bibliographiCitation).

docs.title: Slot: title_type
docs.text: Indica se o título é um nome próprio, descritivo, etc.

docs.title: wasth_schema
docs.text:
Esquemas LinkML para os Documentários da Arquitetura Tradicional.

URI: https://tradicional.arq.br/schema

docs.title: Slot: work_type_condition
docs.text:
Descriptors for objects that are distinguishable by their overall state such as appearance, level of damage, completeness, or quality. If an object is identified by its prevailing physical state, then it is qualified by condition.

Based on AAT "conditions" and CIDOC CRM "E3 Condition State"

Atende aos campos do SICG "estado de preservação" e "estado de conservação".

docs.title: Slot: work_type_context
docs.text:
Descriptors for objects that are distinguishable by their use or application within a particular physical location. If an object is identifiable by association with specific surroundings, it is qualified by location or context.

Based on AAT Guidelines "Types of Guide Terms"

Nos Documentários da Arquitetura Tradicional, designa a situação de implantação da edificação, por exemplo se está em contexto urbano ou rural, isolada ou em correnteza...

docs.title: Slot: work_type_form
docs.text:
Descriptors for objects that are distinguishable by their physical form or by the manner in which they are presented. If an object is identified by sight, then it is qualified by form.

Based on AAT Guidelines "Types of Guide Terms"

Nos Documentários da Arquitetura Tradicional, designa uma tipologia formal.

docs.title: Slot: work_type_function
docs.text:
Objects that are distinguishable by the particular purpose for which they are designed or used. If an object is identifiable by its intended use, then it is qualified by function.

Based on AAT Guidelines "Types of Guide Terms"

Nos Documentários da Arquitetura Tradicional, designa um dos sete tipos de propósitos concebidos por C. William Westfall e Samir Younés em Architectural Type and Character.

docs.title: Slot: work_type_material_tech
docs.text:
Descriptors for objects that are distinguishable by their materials encorporated, or the techniques used to create the object or work. If an object is identified by the substances detected and/or the processes employed, then it is qualified by material or technique.

Nos Documentários da Arquitetura Tradicional, refere-se à caracterização construtiva geral da edificação.

docs.title: Slot: work_type_subject_type
docs.text:
Descriptors for objects that are distinguishable by their topics, themes, or other content of the work. If an object is identified by what it is of or about, then it is qualified by subject.

Based on AAT "subjects"

Nos Documentários da Arquitetura Tradicional, é o único bloco opcional desta seção : ele indica, se houver, uma classificação iconográfica mais específica do que form ou function.

docs.title: Slot: work_type_use
docs.text:
Descriptors for objects that are distinguishable by the way they are employed, occupied, applied, or function. If an object is identifiable by its particular mode of use, it is qualified by use.

Based on AAT "use"

Nos Documentários da Arquitetura Tradicional, designa propriamente a(s) classificação(ões) de usos do solo ou atividades predominante(s) na edificação atualmente.
